function: IGCN-based graph beamformer outputs digital beamforming and RHS holographic amplitudes to minimize BS transmit power under rate constraints and imperfect CSI (p. 6, 9).
system: Downlink MISO mmWave IoV: BS with RHS (64 elements, 16 feeds), single-antenna vehicles, 30 GHz; RHS is a BS-integrated antenna, not an RIS (p. 2, 4, 11).
method: Incremental GCN beamformer trained on a transmit-power and rate-shortfall loss over 8 sequential scenarios, with parameter inheritance (fine-tuning), knowledge replay and weight consolidation (p. 8, 10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: time-varying Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel with Jakes outdated CSI, 1 km two-lane road, 2 paths; 5000 samples per scenario (p. 5, 11).
test_conditions: Trained on 8 scenarios (16 to 2 MVs); tested on unseen MV counts (3 to 15, 18 to 50) and Gipps, Krauss, IDM mobility models (p. 16).
baselines: Phased-array beamforming; non-robust MRT HCBF; EWC, iCaRL, transfer learning; PPO DRL (training cost and latency only); SSRT upper bound (p. 13, 15, 16, 17).
metrics: BS transmit power; approximation ratio versus SSRT optimum (rate satisfaction and power); training episodes to convergence; inference latency (p. 13, 14, 17).
complexity: Order of complexity O(B s^2 C^2) (Eq. 33), graph construction O(2Ms + 3s(s-1)); inference latency below 80 microseconds (p. 11, 17).
q1_support: p. 5: "a time-varying Saleh-Valenzuela scattering model is considered to characterize the mmWave channels"; custom simulator, 3GPP TR 38.901 appears only as one of four references [40]-[43] for it.
q2_support: p. 16: "the trained model is transferred to more congested cases with 18 to 50 MVs"; it was trained on 16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 MVs and also tested on 3 to 15 MVs without retraining.
q3_support: p. 15: "compared with state-of-the-art benchmark methods, namely elastic weight consolidation (EWC), incremental classifier and representation learning (iCARL), and transfer learning (TL)" (approximation ratio); p. 16: "the non-robust HCBF scheme using the maximum ratio transmission (MRT) method" (transmit power).
q4_support: p. 11: "The total computational complexity of the proposed method is" an O(B s^2 C^2) expression (Eq. 33); p. 17: "microsecond-level inference latency".
q5_support: p. 5: "a time-varying Saleh-Valenzuela scattering model"; channels are simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link or DOI and uses no public dataset.
notes: The PDF carries no DOI or journal banner, so its identity with the DOI is not confirmable from the file. ris=0 because p. 2 (footnote 1) says the RHS is a transceiver metasurface antenna, not an RIS; the reviewer may decide otherwise. q3 relies on MRT as the non-learned baseline and on EWC, iCaRL and TL as earlier learning methods applied to the same task (the paper calls them baseline LGL methods, p. 3). Area 3 by function: the learned model outputs beamformers, not hardware design.
